Exercise: Single-Leg Lateral Hop

Category:
plyometrics

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- lateral_hopping

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- abductors
- adductors
- calves
- hamstrings

Equipment:

- other

Fatigue Score:
2

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
high

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- enhance_explosive_power
- improve_unilateral_lower_body_strength_and_stability

Contraindications:
None

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single-Leg Lateral Hop with Medicine Ball, description: Hold a medicine ball during the hop to increase upper body involvement.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Single-Leg Box Hop, reason: similar unilateral lower body movement

Instructions:

- Stand to the side of a cone or hurdle. To get into the start position, stand on one leg with your knee slightly bent.
- To begin, execute a counterjump to hop sideways over the cone.
- Land on your jumping leg, and immediately rebound out of it by jumping back to the start position.
- Continue hopping back and forth.
